instructions.content: Be evidence-only: reference actual prompts and tool calls from the sessions
Quantify always: write ratios such as 3 out of 8 sessions, never vague adjectives
Compare impact against the targets (>60% high-impact augmentation, <20% automation) and surface the gap explicitly when missed
Take a longitudinal view: track skill evolution across sessions, not just a point-in-time snapshot
Step 1: run the session filter script with the user's arguments; the first line is PERIOD and the remaining lines are session paths, so never treat the PERIOD line as a session
Step 2: read sessions and extract user_prompts, tool_calls, duration_seconds, subagent_spawns and JSONL events
Step 3: analyse technical effectiveness across context management, guidance, critical thinking and bias
Step 4: analyse cognitive posture across intentionality, agency, impact and progression
Categorise each session as Automation, Low-impact or High-impact augmentation
Step 5: generate Start/Stop/Continue with specific session examples
Step 6: write insights to the collab insights folder under the PERIOD file name
Step 7: report the output file path and suggest the aggregate report command
Use the Metrics Summary format: sessions, total prompts and average, tool calls and average, duration and subagents, and the impact split against targets
Do not run the skill on fewer than one complete session file, because partial data produces unreliable scores
When duration_seconds is absent from older session files, skip duration metrics rather than erroring
Provide a partial report if some session files are unreadable rather than aborting entirely
NEVER fabricate session evidence
NEVER report a single session as a trend
NEVER skip the impact categorisation step
NEVER use a hardcoded output path
Use retrospect-domain instead when the focus is on WHAT was learned, not HOW the collaboration worked
